prev_agent: Great question — and it's actually two problems stacked on top of each other: **Problem 1: Discovery** — does the agent know the file exists? **Problem 2: Loading** — does the agent actually pull its content into context? Knowing about it and *reading it* are not the same thing. --- ## The Pickup Mechanisms (by reliability) `★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────` Every AI agent has a "context bootstrap" — a set of files it reads automatically before the user types anything. The goal is to get `.code-insights.md` content into that bootstrap, not just leave it sitting on disk hoping the agent notices. `─────────────────────────────────────────────────` ### Tier 1 — Agent reads it without being asked (most reliable) These files are loaded automatically at session start, no instructions needed: | Agent | Auto-loaded file | |-------|-----------------| | Claude Code | `CLAUDE.md` at project root | | Claude Code | `.claude/CLAUDE.md` | | Cursor | `.cursorrules` | | Codex CLI | `AGENTS.md` at project root | | VS Code Copilot | `.github/copilot-instructions.md` | | Windsurf | `.windsurfrules` | If the content of `.code-insights.md` is **inline** in any of these — the agent gets it. Zero failure modes. ### Tier 2 — Agent follows a reference (usually reliable, one failure point) The agent reads `CLAUDE.md`, sees: ``` See .code-insights.md for AI-extracted codebase knowledge. ``` ...and then reads the file. Claude Code is good at this. Cursor sometimes does, sometimes doesn't. It depends on whether the agent treats that as an instruction to follow or just prose to acknowledge. One failure point: the "follow the link" step. If the agent is lazy or rushed or context-constrained, it reads the instruction and moves on without actually loading the file. ### Tier 3 — File discovery (unreliable) Some agents scan the project root for known filenames.
